name: Hoover Dam
notes: Nominal $49M (1931 budget). Wikipedia infobox.

name: Bonneville Dam Ph1
notes: $88.4M per USACE fact sheet / Wikipedia. Phase 1: spillway + 1st powerhouse + lock.

name: Grand Coulee Dam orig
notes: Original dam + L/R powerhouses $163M per Wikipedia. Orig capacity ~2325 MW (18x125 MW units).

name: Shasta Dam
notes: Construction contract ~$36M per Marketplace.org/Bureau of Reclamation. Current nameplate 676-710 MW.

name: Moses-Saunders Dam
notes: 1957 MW combined (RH Saunders 1045 MW + FDR 912 MW). No total construction cost in public sources.

name: Noxon Rapids Dam
notes: Wikipedia infobox. 5 turbines.

name: Robert Moses Niagara
notes: $800M per Wikipedia (1957 cost basis). Was largest hydro in Western hemisphere when opened 1961.

name: Twin Falls GS
notes: Wikipedia infobox; cost denominated in USD. Decommissioned 1974 when Churchill Falls opened.

name: Wanapum Dam
notes: Wikipedia infobox. 10 x 104 MW Kaplan turbines.

name: WAC Bennett Dam
notes: C$750M per Wikipedia. CAD/USD approx 0.93 (1968). 10 Francis turbines.

name: Rocky Reach Dam
notes: Wikipedia infobox. 11 turbines (7x114 + 4x125.4 MW).

name: Churchill Falls GS
notes: C$946M per Wikipedia. CAD/USD approx 0.98 (1974). 11 turbines. 16th largest hydro globally.

name: Grand Coulee 3rd PH
notes: Nathaniel Washington PH only; 6 Francis units (3x690 + 3x805 MW). $730M per Wikipedia (1973 dollars).

name: Mica Dam
notes: Original 1973 cost not published. Units 5&6 expansion (2015) approx C$1B per KWL.ca.

name: Peace Canyon Dam
notes: No construction cost in public sources.

name: Bonneville Dam Ph2
notes: Second powerhouse only (8 generators, 558.2 MW). $664M per Wikipedia.

name: Robert-Bourassa LG-2
notes: C$3.8B (1987 dollars) per Wikipedia. CAD/USD approx 0.76 (1987). James Bay Project. Largest underground powerhouse in world.

name: Itaipu Dam
notes: US$19.6B per Wikipedia. 20 x 700 MW. Largest global hydro until 2011. CF 62.3%.

name: Revelstoke Dam
notes: 2480 MW (5 units; 6th unit approved 2025). No original construction cost in public sources.

name: Limestone GS
notes: C$1.43B per Wikipedia; came in under budget. CAD/USD approx 0.83. 10 x 134 MW Kaplan.

name: La Grande-1 GS
notes: C$2.5B per Wikipedia. CAD/USD approx 0.73. 12 Kaplan turbines; run-of-river.

name: Xiaolangdi Dam
notes: US$3.5B per Wikipedia. World Bank co-financed. 6 x 306 MW Francis.

name: Three Gorges Dam
notes: Y203B = US$31.765B per Wikipedia. Final audit Y249B (~$37B) incl. resettlement. 32 x 700 MW + 2 x 50 MW.

name: Xiluodu Dam
notes: Y50.34B = US$6.2B per Wikipedia / Power Technology. Some sources cite up to $12B. 18 x 770 MW Francis.

name: Liyuan Dam
notes: Y16.2B = US$2.4B per Wikipedia. 4 x 600 MW Francis.

name: Changheba Dam
notes: US$3.46B per Wikipedia. 4 x 650 MW Francis. Rock-fill, 240 m high.

name: Muskrat Falls GS
notes: C$12.7B per Wikipedia (orig est C$7.4B in 2012). CAD/USD approx 0.75. 4 x 206 MW Kaplan. Includes 1100 km HVDC transmission link.

name: Wudongde Dam
notes: Y120B = US$17.47B (2023 equiv per Wikipedia). 12 x 850 MW Francis. 4th largest globally.

name: Baihetan Dam
notes: Y220B = US$31.58B per Wikipedia. 16 x 1000 MW (worlds largest single unit). 2nd largest globally.

name: Keeyask GS
notes: C$8.7B final per CBC/Manitoba Hydro (orig est C$6.5B in 2012). CAD/USD approx 0.78. 7 units; KHLP (MB Hydro 75% + 4 First Nations 25%).

name: Site C John Horgan Dam
notes: C$16B as-spent (2021 estimate; final not yet published). CAD/USD approx 0.79. Orig est C$8.8B (2014). BCs most expensive infrastructure project.
